name: Karsjena
title: One of the seven counselors of the Persian king
summary: Karsjena was one of the seven princes in Persia and Media who had direct access to King Ahasuerus (Xerxes I). These seven wise men were the king's closest advisors and held high positions in the Persian Empire. Karsjena is mentioned in connection with advising on what should be done about Queen Vashti after her disobedience to the king's command.

keyEvents.title: One of the king's seven counselors
keyEvents.description: Carshena is mentioned as the first of the seven princes of Persia and Media who saw the king's face and held the highest seats in the kingdom.

keyEvents.title: Advice regarding Queen Vashti's disobedience
keyEvents.description: When Queen Vashti refused to come at the king's command, King Ahasuerus consulted his seven wise men, including Carshena, about what the law required should be done.

keyEvents.title: The king's banquet and the crisis
keyEvents.description: During the great banquet held by King Ahasuerus in the citadel of Susa, conflict arose with Queen Vashti, leading to Carshena and the other advisors being consulted.

keyEvents.title: Memukan's proposal is adopted
keyEvents.description: After the consultation, Memukan, one of the seven princes along with Carshena, put forward the proposal that Vashti should be stripped of her royal dignity. This paved the way for Esther to later become queen.
